Ran 18 commands, read a page
Two separate bugs, plus your attribute change. None of them were caused by your tweak.

1. Build error. xUnit v3 4.x made CollectionBehavior(DisableTestParallelization = true) obsolete (an error under warnings-as-errors). Its replacement is [assembly: Parallelization(Mode = ParallelMode.None)], using Xunit.v3 and Xunit.Sdk. I checked this against the v3-4.0.2 source.

2. Static assets 404 when the app isn’t started from its publish folder. e2e-container.sh runs dotnet /tmp/app/Chaos.Web.dll from /work. That makes the content root /work, so the web root /work/wwwroot doesn’t exist. As a result blazor.web.js, App.razor.js, app.css and Chaos.Web.styles.css all 404. That explains the trace:

The theme button does nothing because App.razor.js never loaded.
“Something went wrong” is visible because the scoped CSS that hides it never loaded.
The only passing test is the headers/404 one, which needs no JS.
Velixir has the same problem. Nixpacks starts ./out/Chaos.Web from the upload root, so the live site is very likely broken the same way. I fixed it in Program.cs rather than in the script, so E2E keeps running the app the way velixir does. Changing the content root instead would throw under WebApplicationFactory, so the fix only sets the web root.

3. Every WebSocket gets refused, even once JS loads. HubGuard checks context.WebSockets.IsWebSocketRequest. The IHttpWebSocketFeature behind that only exists once UseWebSockets has run. SignalR adds that middleware inside the hub endpoint, after the guard. So the guard always sees false and returns 400, and no circuit can open. The unit test didn’t catch this because TestServer injects its own WebSocket feature. The fix is app.UseWebSockets() before the guard; SignalR’s inner copy then skips because the feature already exists.

I also made the E2E script print the tail of the app log when tests fail.

Nothing to delete.

src/Chaos.Web/Program.cs
csharp
using System.IO.Compression;
using Chaos.Web.Components;
using Chaos.Web.Drawing;
using Chaos.Web.Infrastructure;
using Chaos.Web.Messages;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Antiforgery;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.HttpOverrides;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.RateLimiting;
using Microsoft.AspNetCore.ResponseCompression;
using Microsoft.Extensions.Options;

var publishedWebRoot = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "wwwroot");
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(new WebApplicationOptions
{
    Args = args,
    WebRootPath = Directory.Exists(publishedWebRoot) ? publishedWebRoot : null,
});

builder.WebHost.ConfigureKestrel(kestrel =>
{
    kestrel.AddServerHeader = false;
    if (int.TryParse(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("PORT"), out var port))
    {
        kestrel.ListenAnyIP(port);
    }
});

builder.Services.Configure<HostOptions>(host => host.ShutdownTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10));
builder.Services.Configure<ForwardedHeadersOptions>(forwarded =>
{
    forwarded.ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto;
    forwarded.KnownIPNetworks.Clear();
    forwarded.KnownProxies.Clear();
});

builder.Services.AddOptions<ChaosOptions>()
    .Bind(builder.Configuration.GetSection(ChaosOptions.SectionName))
    .Validate(chaos => chaos.IsValid(), "Chaos limits are out of range.")
    .ValidateOnStart();

builder.Services.AddDataProtection().UseEphemeralDataProtectionProvider();
builder.Services.AddSingleton<IAntiforgery>(new CookielessAntiforgery());
builder.Services.AddSingleton(TimeProvider.System);
builder.Services.AddSingleton<BoardService>();
builder.Services.AddSingleton<CanvasService>();
builder.Services.AddSingleton<ConnectionTracker>();
builder.Services.AddHealthChecks();

builder.Services.AddResponseCompression(compression =>
{
    compression.EnableForHttps = true;
    compression.Providers.Add<BrotliCompressionProvider>();
    compression.Providers.Add<GzipCompressionProvider>();
});
builder.Services.Configure<BrotliCompressionProviderOptions>(brotli => brotli.Level = CompressionLevel.Fastest);
builder.Services.Configure<GzipCompressionProviderOptions>(gzip => gzip.Level = CompressionLevel.Fastest);

builder.Services.AddRateLimiter(_ => { });
builder.Services.AddOptions<RateLimiterOptions>()
    .Configure<IOptions<ChaosOptions>>((limiter, chaos) => RequestLimits.Configure(limiter, chaos.Value));

builder.Services.AddRazorComponents()
    .AddInteractiveServerComponents(circuit =>
    {
        circuit.DisconnectedCircuitMaxRetained = 20;
        circuit.DisconnectedCircuitRetentionPeriod = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1);
        circuit.PersistedCircuitInMemoryMaxRetained = 20;
        circuit.PersistedCircuitInMemoryRetentionPeriod = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
        circuit.MaxBufferedUnacknowledgedRenderBatches = 2;
        circuit.JSInteropDefaultCallTimeout = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30);
    })
    .AddHubOptions(hub => hub.MaximumReceiveMessageSize = 32 * 1024);

var app = builder.Build();

app.UseForwardedHeaders();
app.UseSecurityHeaders();

if (!app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseExceptionHandler("/Error", createScopeForErrors: true);
    app.UseHsts();
}

app.UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute("/not-found", createScopeForStatusCodePages: true);
app.UseResponseCompression();
app.UseRateLimiter();
app.UseWebSockets();
app.UseHubGuard();
app.UseAntiforgery();

app.MapHealthChecks("/health");
app.MapStaticAssets();
app.MapRazorComponents<App>()
    .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode(server => server.DisableWebSocketCompression = true);

await app.RunAsync();

public partial class Program;
tests/Chaos.E2E/BrowserFixture.cs
csharp
using Microsoft.Playwright;
using Xunit.Sdk;
using Xunit.v3;

[assembly: Parallelization(Mode = ParallelMode.None)]

namespace Chaos.E2E;

public sealed class BrowserFixture : IAsyncLifetime
{
    private IPlaywright? _playwright;
    private IBrowser? _browser;

    public static string BaseUrl { get; } = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("CHAOS_BASE_URL") ?? "http://127.0.0.1:5080/";

    public async ValueTask InitializeAsync()
    {
        _playwright = await Playwright.CreateAsync();
        _browser = await _playwright.Chromium.LaunchAsync();
    }

    public async ValueTask DisposeAsync()
    {
        if (_browser is not null)
        {
            await _browser.DisposeAsync();
        }

        _playwright?.Dispose();
    }

    public Task<IBrowserContext> NewContextAsync(ColorScheme scheme = ColorScheme.Light)
    {
        var browser = _browser ?? throw new InvalidOperationException("The browser is not running.");
        return browser.NewContextAsync(new BrowserNewContextOptions { BaseURL = BaseUrl, ColorScheme = scheme });
    }
}
scripts/e2e-container.sh
bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

export DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1
export DOTNET_NOLOGO=1
export TESTINGPLATFORM_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1

port=5080
work=/work
app=/tmp/app

mkdir -p "$work"
tar -C /src \
    --exclude=./.git --exclude=./artifacts \
    --exclude='*/bin' --exclude='*/obj' --exclude='*/node_modules' \
    -cf - . | tar -C "$work" -xf -
cd "$work"

dotnet publish src/Chaos.Web --configuration Release --output "$app"

ASPNETCORE_URLS="http://127.0.0.1:$port" \
ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Production \
Chaos__BoardCapacity=5 \
Chaos__PostBurst=1000 \
Chaos__PostsPerSecond=1000 \
Chaos__ResetBurst=1000 \
Chaos__ResetsPerSecond=1000 \
Chaos__MaxConnectionsPerClient=50 \
Chaos__RequestBurst=100000 \
Chaos__RequestsPerSecond=100000 \
    dotnet "$app/Chaos.Web.dll" >/out/app.log 2>&1 &
server=$!
trap 'kill "$server" 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT

ready=false
for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
    if (exec 3<>"/dev/tcp/127.0.0.1/$port") 2>/dev/null; then
        ready=true
        break
    fi
    sleep 1
done

if [ "$ready" != true ]; then
    printf 'error: the app did not start\n' >&2
    cat /out/app.log >&2
    exit 1
fi

status=0
CHAOS_BASE_URL="http://127.0.0.1:$port/" \
    dotnet test --project tests/Chaos.E2E --configuration Release --results-directory /out/results || status=$?

if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
    printf '\n==> Last 50 lines of the app log\n' >&2
    tail -n 50 /out/app.log >&2
fi

exit "$status"
docs/adr/0003-deploy-only-the-web-project.md
markdown
# 0003 Deploy only the web project

Status: accepted

velixir builds with a Nixpacks-style plan: `dotnet restore` and `dotnet publish -c Release -o out` at the upload root, then starts `./out/<first csproj>`. Uploading the repository root would restore, build and publish the test projects too, including the Playwright driver, onto a 1 GB disk.

- The deploy workflow runs `velixir deploy --app <id> --source-dir ./src/Chaos.Web`, the documented monorepo option.
- `Chaos.Web.csproj` is self-sufficient: target framework, nullable, implicit usings and runtime settings are in the project, not only in `Directory.Build.props`. `global.json`, central package management and analyzers do not reach the velixir build, which is fine because the project has no package references.
- The start command runs from the upload root, so the content root is the source folder, not `out/`. The web root is set to `wwwroot` next to the assembly when it exists, so published assets are served. The content root is left alone because `WebApplicationFactory` sets it.
- The app binds to `PORT` when set, like zen.
- Deploys are not gated on CI, matching zen. A failing velixir build keeps the previous release; the `/health` probe stops a release that does not start.
docs/adr/0008-abuse-limits.md
markdown
# 0008 Rate and connection limits

Status: accepted

Defaults live in `ChaosOptions` and can be overridden with `Chaos__*` environment variables. velixir's edge limits sit in front of these.

| Limit | Default |
| --- | --- |
| HTTP requests per client | 120 burst, 10 per second |
| WebSocket connections per client | 8 |
| WebSocket connections in total | 80, then 503 |
| Posts per client | 3 burst, 1 every 2 s |
| Message length | 500 |
| Offered messages per circuit | 50 |
| Stroke points per circuit | 4,000 burst, 1,500 per second |
| Points per batch / stroke / canvas | 256 / 2,048 / 20,000 |
| Resets | 1 s global cooldown, 2 burst per client |

- A client is its IP after `X-Forwarded-For`, or its /64 for IPv6.
- The hub (`/_blazor`) only accepts WebSocket connections, so connection counts are real. Clients behind proxies that block WebSockets cannot use the board or canvas.
- `UseWebSockets` runs before the hub guard. SignalR adds it only inside the hub endpoint, so without it the guard sees no WebSocket requests and refuses every circuit. TestServer supplies its own WebSocket feature and cannot catch this; Playwright does.
- The total cap protects the 256 MB container: zen ran out of memory near 100 circuits.
- In-circuit limits use a `TimeProvider` token bucket so tests are deterministic. HTTP limits use ASP.NET Core's rate limiter.
- There is no moderation. The About page says plainly that content spreads to every client and cannot be recalled.
docs/adr/0014-testing.md
markdown
# 0014 Test strategy

Status: accepted

- .NET: xUnit v3 (package `xunit.v3` 4.x) on Microsoft Testing Platform v2, enabled for `dotnet test` in `global.json`. Unit tests cover services and helpers; integration tests use `WebApplicationFactory` for pages, headers, cookies, the hub guard and compression.
- JavaScript: Vitest in Node tests the pure exports of each module. DOM, IndexedDB, canvas and WebSocket behaviour is covered by Playwright, so no DOM library is installed.
- End to end: Playwright .NET in `mcr.microsoft.com/playwright/dotnet:v<version>-noble`, which ships the .NET 10 SDK and browsers. The version comes from `Directory.Packages.props` only. The app is published and run inside the same container on localhost, in Production mode with relaxed limits. It is started from the source copy, not its publish folder, like velixir starts it. The app log is printed when tests fail and kept in `artifacts/e2e/app.log`.
- End-to-end tests run serially (`[assembly: Parallelization(Mode = ParallelMode.None)]`) because they share one server's board and canvas. `CollectionBehavior.DisableTestParallelization` is obsolete in xUnit v3 4.x.
- Coverage is reported (Cobertura for .NET and JavaScript) with no threshold.
- Test projects use the default analyzer set; the app uses the recommended set. Warnings are errors everywhere.
I couldn’t build or run any of this here, because the sandbox can’t reach the .NET download hosts. Each fix is checked against the aspnetcore and xunit sources on GitHub.

If E2E still fails, the last 50 lines of artifacts/e2e/app.log will now be printed at the end of the run; send me those.
